record.paper_title: Open problems on countable dense homogeneity
record.context_brief: absolute CDH metric space of size aleph_1
record.original_question: Is there an absolute example of a countable dense homogeneous metric space whose cardinality is aleph_1?

evidence.quote: Problem 6’. Is there an absolute example of a CDH metric space of cardinality ω1?
Both Problems 6 and 6’ were solved in the affirmative by Farah, Hrušák and Martínez Ranero [25].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A separable metric space $X$ is called countable dense homogeneous (CDH) if for any two countable dense subsets $D_1, D_2 \subseteq X$ there exists a homeomorphism $h : X \to X$ with $h(D_1) = D_2$. Such an example is called absolute if its CDH property is provable in ZFC (i.e., does not depend on additional set-theoretic axioms beyond ZFC).

Question: Does there exist, provably in ZFC, a countable dense homogeneous metric space of cardinality $\aleph_1$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question was answered in the affirmative by Farah, Hrušák, and Martínez-Ranero, who constructed in ZFC a countable dense homogeneous metric subspace of the real line of cardinality $\aleph_1$.
